Reasoning: The question asks, when the switch is closed, the potential difference across the 15Ω resistor is equal to the potential difference across which resistor. Therefore the 15Ω and 30Ω resistors are connected between the same two nodes, which is a parallel relationship. The potential difference across parallel components is the same, so the potential difference across the 15Ω resistor is equal to the potential difference across the 30Ω resistor.

method.method_draft: First inspect the circuit diagram: the battery and ammeter are on the left in series with a 20Ω resistor along the top wire. After the 20Ω resistor, the top wire reaches a junction that connects downward through a 15Ω resistor and also continues right to a 30Ω resistor. When the switch at the bottom right is closed, the lower end of the 30Ω resistor is connected to the same bottom return wire as the lower end of the 15Ω resistor. From the text, identify that the question asks which resistor has the same potential difference as the 15Ω resistor when the switch is closed. Use the rule that circuit elements connected between the same two nodes are in parallel and therefore have the same potential difference. Since the 15Ω and 30Ω resistors share the same top node and, with the switch closed, the same bottom node, answer: the 30Ω resistor.
